label: Prioritize each request using MoSCoW
prompt: A small team is building a class sign-up app for launch next month. Sort each request the way a product owner would.

items.task: Students can create an account and sign up for a class
items.explanation: The core action the entire app exists for. Without this, there's no product — it's the definition of a Must have.

items.task: Students get a confirmation email after signing up
items.explanation: Important for trust and reducing support questions, but the app technically still functions at launch without it — sign-ups would just be silent.

items.task: Students can add a class to their personal calendar with one click
items.explanation: A genuinely nice convenience, but nobody is blocked without it — a classic Could have, first to cut if the deadline tightens.

items.task: A full native mobile app, in addition to the website
items.explanation: A much larger undertaking than the current scope calls for. Naming it Won't have (this time) — rather than ignoring it — keeps it from resurfacing in every planning conversation.

items.task: Instructors can see a live list of who has signed up for their class
items.explanation: Without this, instructors have no way to actually run their class — it's core functionality, not a nice-to-have.

items.task: Students can leave a star rating and review after a class ends
items.explanation: Adds value over time but has zero impact on whether sign-ups work at launch — a reasonable Could have for a later release.
